articles.title: Wrinkled Lacquer
articles.summary: Dense, fine periodic spec texture with strong checker-like clearcoat blocks; high-contrast micro relief across most of the surface. A busy checkered grain with small slanted flickers; the tiles blur into a rough, crinkled sheen that is still obviously textured.
articles.what: Wrinkled Lacquer assembles compressed lacquer ridges, fold crest splits, polished wrinkle shoulders, cross fold creases and trapped coat bubbles. Up close: A square tile grid, tiles about 25 px, outlined by thin bright seams, each tile holding a bold slanted wrinkle fold and curly crease marks. The tile lines are crisp on metallic, softer on satin; folds read as dark curls outside the highlight and bright slashes inside it. From a distance: A busy checkered grain with small slanted flickers; the tiles blur into a rough, crinkled sheen that is still obviously textured. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Crack & Weather (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Crack & Weather", or search for "Wrinkled Lacquer".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors for a rugged all-over look
Avoid small panels and fine graphics, it overwhelms
Numbers stay readable but the tile grid and folds are busy behind them; use big bold numbers.
Bright slanted wrinkle slashes in the highlight inside a faint tile grid; rugged crinkled satin
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not a paint crackle or crocodile skin: tidy tiles with fold marks, shine only, no colour
Not Snake Scale Diamond: tiles carry curly fold marks and darker lines, not just seams
Avoid: very busy, avoid on small panels, can overwhelm fine graphics.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Wrinkled Lacquer over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Zone Plate Shards
articles.summary: Fine broken plate shards scatter micro glints; low-contrast, softly anisotropic sheen with recessed focal pits. A sparse, busy dotted grain with a regular repeat; shards blur out into a faint tiled sparkle.
articles.what: Zone Plate Shards assembles broken zone plate sectors, sector facet boundaries, shard edge losses, recessed focus arclets and detached plate grains. Up close: A neat square grid of separate shard clusters, about 30 px, each an angular broken leaf-like fragment with curved arc lines and a small square chip beside it, with a lot of smooth ground between clusters. Satin shows bright glinting facets; metallic shows dull shard shapes on bright metal. From a distance: A sparse, busy dotted grain with a regular repeat; shards blur out into a faint tiled sparkle. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Optical & Interference (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, trim, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Optical & Interference", or search for "Zone Plate Shards".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and hero panels; the open ground between shards keeps it airy
Numbers stay readable; the sparse shards leave plenty of clean ground, so legibility is good.
Bright faceted shard glints inside the highlight on a plain ground; sparkly but clean
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not Stress Star Crazing: separate spaced clusters in a grid, not a dense shard field
Not ceramic glaze paint: shine only, no colour
Avoid: large flat panels where pattern reads as dirt, very glossy bases that drown the micro glints.

articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.
